versions.changes: Start-up checks: the start-up window now appears only when a check fails, and a new check looks on GitHub for a newer version; when there is one, a bar under the top menu says so (Update / Dismiss) and a dot appears by the version number. Being offline is not a failure. Line of credit: the balance starts at $0, taking money out makes it negative and counts as owed, payments bring it back to $0, and an overpayment is a positive balance that does not reduce other liabilities (credit cards are unchanged); “Real balance today” and “Opening balance” replace the owed wording (owing $10,000 is -10000) and existing lines are converted. Transactions lists (Spending and Transactions): a tick box on every line and a select-all box; the Edit, Split and Delete buttons are gone from the lines. Ticking one line shows its Edit / Split / Delete bar under it; ticking several shows a bar at the bottom with the count, Change category (Spending entries; the merchants are remembered) and Delete, and Shift-click selects a range. Accounts page: Investment accounts and Chequing and savings accounts are separate tables with only the columns that apply (Name, Type, Ownership, value or interest rate, cash, % of net worth); every table is read-only until you click a row, which opens an edit bar with the other fields (account ID, real cash today, closed, ignore in net worth, transaction count, Delete); chequing and savings accounts have an Ownership setting and can be deleted together with their imported entries, as can credit cards and lines of credit; chequing and savings are no longer listed under Assets here (they still count in the Overview’s asset total). Assets and Liabilities work the same way. Margin page: Margin interest takes a third of the width next to the monthly card, same height, hiding Statement dates and then stacking on narrow windows. Spending chart: clicking a daily point opens that day; the card titles above the charts are removed; Transactions remembers whether you last viewed Spending or Investing. Retirement: the year-by-year table no longer has scroll bars.

Update from GitHub: the Update page shows the installed version and the newest published version, lists every version in the public releases repository (DarrenS01/InvestTrackerApp_public) and lets you choose any of them, including an older one. You confirm first; your data is backed up, the file is downloaded and checked against its SHA-256, then installed and the program restarts. The packaged program takes the ready-made InvestTracker.exe when one is published (no Python needed) and otherwise builds from the source zip as before. A GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) builds the Windows exe and publishes it with the source zip and index.json whenever tracker/version.py changes on main (needs the PUBLIC_REPO_TOKEN secret). Choosing a file on the Update page still works.
